title: Working at French ski resorts on a visa saisonnier: a guide for Latin Americans
shortAnswer: Short answer: the resorts in the French Alps hire thousands of people every winter, above all in hotels and restaurants, from December to April. From Latin America you can work on a visa saisonnier if a French employer hires you and applies for your autorisation de travail. Because the process takes several weeks, you have to start months before the season.

blocks.text: The big groups have already announced their hiring campaigns. Club Med, for example, opened more than 1,400 positions at its Alpine resorts this winter, 840 of them in hotels and restaurants. La Plagne alone needs more than 3,000 people every season. Many offers are “logées”: the employer provides the housing, sometimes with a contribution toward the rent.
English helps a lot: the clientele is international. Basic French opens even more doors.
A realistic timeline from Latin America

items: 6 to 4 months before: find an employer and sign the seasonal contract (3 months minimum).
4 to 2 months before: the employer applies for the autorisation de travail.
2 months before: consulate appointment for the 3-month visa saisonnier.
On arrival: you apply for your carte travailleur saisonnier at the préfecture.

blocks.text: For the 2026-2027 winter season it is already too late if you are outside France. The smart move is to prepare for the summer of 2027 (grape harvests, beach tourism) or the 2027-2028 winter.

items: France Travail, in its seasonal work section.
The job pages of each resort (Courchevel, Méribel, Val Thorens, Tignes, Les Deux Alpes).
The hotel and holiday groups that hire in large numbers.
Seasonal job fairs, which are held from the fall onwards.

items.question: Can I stay after the season?
items.answer: Not on the visa saisonnier: the maximum is 6 months a year in France, and then you have to go back to your country.

items.question: Do I need experience?
items.answer: For many kitchen, cleaning or sales positions, no. For skiman or chef, yes.

items.question: Is the housing free?
items.answer: It depends: some employers cover it in full and others ask for a contribution. Check it in your contract.
